faqs.question: Is Morocco or Turkey cheaper?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent value, but Turkey is currently cheaper overall due to the Turkish lira's depreciation. A mid-range day in Morocco runs $60-90 USD; Turkey runs $50-80 USD. faqs.answer: Morocco is the top Sahara destination in North Africa for tourists. The Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga are extraordinary — towering 150m orange dunes accessible from Marrakech on a 3-day circuit. faqs.question: Is Morocco safe for solo female travelers?
faqs.answer: Morocco requires more research and preparation for solo female travelers than Turkey. Harassment in medinas (persistent vendors, unwanted attention) is a common complaint on r/solotravel and r/travel. faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Morocco vs Turkey?
faqs.answer: Morocco: March-May and September-November are ideal — mild weather, manageable crowds. Summer is very hot inland (Marrakech can hit 42°C in July). Sahara is best October-April. faqs.answer: Both are world-class food cultures. Morocco's cuisine — tagines, couscous, bastilla, harira, merguez, preserved lemons, ras el hanout — is richly spiced, slow-cooked, and extraordinary. faqs.question: Do I need a visa for Morocco or Turkey?
faqs.answer: Most Western passport holders (US, EU, UK, Canada, Australia) can enter both Morocco and Turkey without a pre-arranged visa for 90 days. faqs.question: Can you visit both Morocco and Turkey in one trip?
faqs.answer: Yes — they're about 4 hours apart by direct flight from Casablanca or Marrakech to Istanbul. A 3-week combo (10 days Morocco + 10 days Turkey) is very manageable. Some travelers combine them via Spain (Madrid-Marrakech, then Madrid-Istanbul), turning it into a broader Southern Europe / North Africa
